newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Publishers group blasts Peru on press freedom.
newsitem.headline: Publishers group blasts Peru on press freedom.

text.p: The Interamerican Press Association (IAPA) on Thursday called on Peru's government to reverse its decision to strip an Israeli-born television station owner of his citizenship.
Peru's controversial move, which came after the TV station aired a report alleging widespread phone-tapping by the government, was called a setback to press freedom by the IAPA.

"We have pointed out what it would mean if they didn't review the decision to revoke his citizenship, the risks it would have for Peru's image as state ruled by law," Danilo Arbilla of IAPA's Press Freedom Commisison told Reuters.

Arbilla, editor of the Uruguayan business weekly Busqueda, said a police chief revoked the Peruvian citizenship of television station owner Baruch Ivcher after his station aired a report on phone-tapping by Peru's security services.

Peruvian officials said Ivcher was stripped of his Peruvian citizenship not because of the allegations aired by the station, but because he had not complied with a requirement to renounce his Israeli citizenship.
More than 50 percent of the phones tapped belonged to journalists, Arbilla said. The commission also found other limitations on press freedom in Peru.

"In Peru a series of acts during the past six to seven months has affected full press freedom," Arbilla said. He said Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori strongly denied there was any plan to intimidate journalists.
